topics.title: Introduction, Residuary Scope & Method of Accounting
explain: Income from Other Sources (IFOS) is the residuary head of income.
Any taxable income that does not fit into the other four specific heads is taxed here.
Income under IFOS is computed using either cash or mercantile system of accounting.
The assessee must regularly follow the chosen accounting method.

flow.title: Determining Taxability Under IFOS
steps: Check if receipt is taxable income
Check if it fits under first 4 heads
If not covered under other heads, route to IFOS
Apply cash or mercantile accounting method

topics.example: A person receives interest on a personal loan given to a friend. Since this does not fall under Salaries, House Property, PGBP, or Capital Gains, it is taxed under IFOS.
remember: IFOS acts as a catch-all head for taxable income.
Method of accounting (cash or mercantile) must be regularly employed.
mistakes: Assuming all receipts are taxable under IFOS even if they are non-taxable capital receipts.

quiz.q: Which accounting method can be regularly employed for computing IFOS?
quiz.why: Under Section 276, income under IFOS can be computed on either cash or mercantile basis as regularly employed.

quiz.q: Why is IFOS called the residuary head of income?
o: It is calculated first before all other heads
It taxes all income not specifically covered under other heads
It only applies to corporate assessees
quiz.why: Section 92(1) brings to tax any income that cannot be included under any of the preceding specific heads.

topics.title: Dividend Income & Deemed Dividend
explain: Dividend income is always taxable under the head IFOS.
Deemed dividend u/s 2(40)(a) includes asset distribution entailing release of company assets.
Deemed dividend u/s 2(40)(b) covers distribution of debentures, deposit certificates, or bonus shares to preference shareholders.
Deemed dividend u/s 2(40)(c) & (d) includes distribution on liquidation or capital reduction to the extent of accumulated profits.
Deemed dividend u/s 2(40)(e) covers loans/advances given by a closely held company to a beneficial shareholder holding at least 10% voting power, limited to accumulated profits.
Trade advances in commercial transactions are not deemed dividends as per CBDT Circular 19/2017.

flow.title: Testing Loans/Advances for Deemed Dividend u/s 2(40)(e)
steps: Check if company is closely held
Check if recipient shareholder holds >= 10% voting power
Verify loan is not a commercial trade advance
Tax as deemed dividend up to accumulated profits

topics.example: Alpha Pvt. Ltd., a closely held firm with accumulated profits of Rs. 10 lakhs, gives a personal loan of Rs. 15 lakhs to Mr. Raj (14% shareholder). Rs. 10 lakhs is taxable as deemed dividend u/s 2(40)(e).
remember: Bonus shares to equity shareholders are NOT treated as dividend.
Deemed dividend u/s 2(40)(e) is capped at accumulated profits.
mistakes: Taxing the entire loan amount u/s 2(40)(e) even when it exceeds company's accumulated profits.

quiz.q: XYZ Ltd. issues bonus shares to its equity shareholders out of accumulated profits. What is the tax treatment?
quiz.why: Bonus shares given to equity shareholders are not treated as dividend under tax law.

quiz.q: A closely held company gives a loan of Rs. 12 lakhs to a 15% shareholder. Accumulated profits are Rs. 8 lakhs. What is the deemed dividend?
quiz.why: Deemed dividend under section 2(40)(e) is restricted to the extent of accumulated profits of the company.

topics.title: Casual Income & Online Game Winnings
explain: Casual income includes winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, races, card games, gambling, and betting.
Casual income (other than online games) is taxed at a flat rate of 30% plus surcharge and 4% cess.
Net winnings from online games are taxed at 30% plus surcharge and 4% cess u/s 194(1) (Table: Sl. No. 5).
No expenses or allowances are allowed against casual income or online game winnings.
Chapter VIII deductions and basic exemption limit set-off are strictly prohibited against such winnings.

flow.title: Tax Computation on Casual Income
steps: Identify lottery, betting, or game winnings
Separate online game net winnings if applicable
Disallow all related expenses and Chapter VIII deductions
Apply flat tax rate of 30% plus cess

topics.example: An individual wins Rs. 1,00,000 in a lottery ticket scheme and spends Rs. 2,000 on tickets. The taxable income is Rs. 1,00,000 taxed at 30% plus cess without deducting Rs. 2,000.
remember: Flat 30% tax rate applies without basic exemption adjustment.
Zero expense deduction allowed against casual winnings.
mistakes: Deducting the cost of lottery tickets or game entry fees from winnings.

quiz.q: What is the flat rate of tax on lottery winnings?
quiz.why: Winnings from lotteries are taxed at a flat rate of 30% plus applicable surcharge and 4% health & education cess.

quiz.q: Can an assessee adjust unexhausted basic exemption limit against lottery winnings?
quiz.why: Adjustment of unexhausted basic exemption limit is strictly not permitted against casual income.

topics.title: Advance Forfeited for Capital Asset Transfer
explain: Advance money received and forfeited during negotiations for transfer of a capital asset is taxable under IFOS.
This applies if such sum is forfeited on or after 1st April 2026 and negotiations fail.
Such forfeited advance is not deducted from the cost of acquisition of the asset.
Advances forfeited prior to 1st April 2014 were reduced from the cost of acquisition when computing capital gains.

flow.title: Processing Forfeited Advance Money
steps: Receive advance money for capital asset transfer
Negotiation fails to materialize into transfer
Forfeit the advance sum
Tax entire forfeited amount under IFOS

topics.example: Mr. A received an advance of Rs. 6 lakhs in May 2026 for selling land. The deal failed and Mr. A forfeited the amount. Rs. 6 lakhs is fully taxable under IFOS.
remember: Advance forfeited on or after 1.4.2026 goes to IFOS.
Cost of acquisition of the asset remains unadjusted.
mistakes: Reducing the forfeited advance from the purchase cost of the land when sold later.

quiz.q: Where is advance money forfeited on 20th May 2026 during land sale negotiations taxed?
quiz.why: Section 92(2)(h) provides that advance money forfeited on or after 1st April 2026 is taxable under IFOS.

quiz.q: How does advance money forfeited in 2026 affect the cost of acquisition of the capital asset?
o: It reduces the cost of acquisition
It increases the cost of acquisition
It has no effect on cost of acquisition
It doubles the cost of acquisition
quiz.why: Forfeited advances taxable under IFOS are not reduced from the cost of acquisition for capital gains.

topics.title: Interest on Compensation / Enhanced Compensation
explain: Interest received on compensation or enhanced compensation is deemed to be income of the tax year in which it is received.
It is taxable under IFOS regardless of the method of accounting followed by the assessee.
A flat deduction of 50% of such interest received is allowed u/s 93(1)(f).
No other expense (such as legal fees) is deductible from this interest income.

flow.title: Taxing Enhanced Compensation Interest
steps: Receive interest on enhanced compensation
Tax entire amount in year of receipt
Deduct 50% flat allowance u/s 93(1)(f)
Charge remaining 50% to tax under IFOS

topics.example: Mr. G receives Rs. 5,00,000 as enhanced compensation interest in T.Y. 2026-27. After 50% deduction (Rs. 2,50,000), Rs. 2,50,000 is chargeable to tax under IFOS.
remember: Taxable strictly in the year of RECEIPT.
Flat 50% deduction is allowed; legal expenses are ignored.
mistakes: Spreading the interest income back to the previous years to which it relates.

quiz.q: In which year is interest on enhanced compensation taxable?
o: Tax year in which it is received
quiz.why: Section 278(1) mandates that interest on enhanced compensation is taxable in the year of receipt.

quiz.q: What deduction percentage is allowed against interest on enhanced compensation?
quiz.why: Section 93(1)(f) allows a flat 50% deduction of such interest income.

topics.title: Termination Compensation & Life Insurance Receipts
explain: Compensation for employment termination/modification received from a non-employer is taxed under IFOS u/s 92(2)(j).
Sum received under a Life Insurance Policy (LIP) not excluded under Schedule II is taxable u/s 92(2)(l).
For policies issued on or after 1.4.2023, exemption is unavailable if aggregate annual premium exceeds Rs. 5,00,000 in any TY.
Sum received on the death of an insured person remains fully exempt.
Rule 59 prescribes taxable income as receipts minus aggregate un-deducted premiums paid over policy term.

flow.title: Testing LIP Maturity Receipts for Exemption
steps: Check if amount received is on death
If on death, claim full exemption
If on maturity, check issue date & premium limit
If premium > Rs. 5,00,000, compute taxable part via Rule 59

topics.example: A policy issued on 1.4.2023 has an annual premium of Rs. 6,00,000. Upon maturity, the proceeds are not exempt under Schedule II because annual premium exceeds Rs. 5,00,000.
remember: Death benefit is ALWAYS exempt.
Rs. 5,00,000 premium cap applies to policies issued on or after 1.4.2023.
mistakes: Treating maturity receipts of LIPs with premium over Rs. 5,00,000 as fully exempt.

quiz.q: What is the annual premium limit for LIP exemption issued on or after 1.4.2023?
quiz.why: Exemption under Schedule II for LIPs issued on/after 1.4.2023 requires total annual premium not exceeding Rs. 5,00,000.

quiz.q: Are sums received on the death of an insured person under a LIP taxable?
quiz.why: Any sum received on the death of a person is exempt regardless of annual premium paid.

topics.title: Taxability of Gifts - Money and Property
explain: Gifts of money received without consideration exceeding Rs. 50,000 in aggregate in a year are fully taxable.
Immovable property received without consideration is taxable if Stamp Duty Value (SDV) exceeds Rs. 50,000.
Immovable property received for inadequate consideration is taxable if (SDV - Consideration) exceeds higher of Rs. 50,000 or 10% of consideration.
Movable specified property (shares, jewellery, paintings, bullion, etc.) is taxable if FMV or (FMV - Consideration) exceeds Rs. 50,000.
Gifts from defined relatives, on occasion of individual's marriage, under a will/inheritance, or from registered NPOs are fully EXEMPT.

flow.title: Gift Taxability Decision Tree
steps: Check if receipt is from a defined relative
If from relative or on marriage, exempt fully
If from non-relative, check asset type and value thresholds
If threshold exceeded, tax under IFOS

topics.example: Ms. Riya receives Rs. 48,000 cash from Friend A and Rs. 10,000 from Friend B. Since total cash gift (Rs. 58,000) exceeds Rs. 50,000, the whole Rs. 58,000 is taxable under IFOS.
remember: Relative definition includes spouse, siblings, lineal ascendants/descendants, and their spouses.
Cars and furniture are NOT in specified property list, so gifting them is non-taxable.
mistakes: Taxing only the excess amount over Rs. 50,000 instead of the whole sum once threshold is crossed.

quiz.q: Ms. Riya receives Rs. 48,000 and Rs. 10,000 cash gifts from two friends. What amount is taxable under IFOS?
quiz.why: Since aggregate money gifts exceed Rs. 50,000, the entire sum of Rs. 58,000 is taxable under section 92(2)(m).

quiz.q: Which of the following items is NOT included in specified movable property u/s 92(2)(m)?
quiz.why: Motor cars are not included in the definition of 'property' u/s 92(2)(m), so gifting a car is non-taxable.

topics.title: Incomes Chargeable under IFOS if not under PGBP & Exemptions
explain: Employee contributions to PF/ESI received by employer are taxed under IFOS if not charged under PGBP.
Hiring income from plant, machinery, or furniture (and inseparable building letting) is taxed under IFOS if not PGBP.
Interest on securities and Keyman insurance policy receipts are taxed under IFOS if not under PGBP/Salaries.
Salary received by Members of Parliament (MPs/MLAs) is chargeable under IFOS.
Post Office Savings Bank interest is exempt up to Rs. 3,500 (individual) or Rs. 7,000 (joint account).
Disaster relief compensation from government is exempt if no loss deduction was claimed earlier.

flow.title: Testing Income for IFOS vs PGBP
steps: Identify specific income (e.g. machinery hire)
Check if assessee carries on business of such activity
If business activity, tax under PGBP
If not business activity, tax under IFOS

topics.example: An individual owns a generator for personal use and lets it out occasionally on hire. The hire income is taxable under IFOS as it is not a business activity.
remember: MP/MLA salary is taxed under IFOS, not under Salaries.
Post Office Savings Bank interest exemption cap: Rs. 3,500 / Rs. 7,000.
mistakes: Classifying salary of Members of Parliament under the head Salaries.

quiz.q: Under which head is salary received by a Member of Parliament (MP) taxable?
quiz.why: There is no employer-employee relationship, so MP salary is taxed under Income from Other Sources u/s 92.

quiz.q: What is the maximum exemption limit for interest on an individual Post Office Savings Bank Account under Schedule II?
quiz.why: Interest on Post Office Savings Bank Account is exempt up to Rs. 3,500 for an individual account.

topics.title: Deductions Allowable
explain: Commission or remuneration paid to bankers for realizing interest on securities is deductible.
Employee PF/ESI contributions remitted before due date u/s 263(1) are deductible.
Repairs, insurance, and depreciation are deductible against machinery, plant, furniture, or building hire income.
Family pension standard deduction is 1/3rd of pension or Rs. 15,000 (optional regime) / Rs. 25,000 (default regime u/s 202), whichever is less.
Revenue expenditure incurred wholly and exclusively for earning IFOS income is allowed.
No deduction is allowed against dividend income, mutual fund unit income, or casual winnings.

flow.title: Computing Deduction for Family Pension
steps: Receive family pension amount
Calculate 1/3rd of the pension received
Compare with Rs. 25,000 (default) or Rs. 15,000 (optional)
Deduct lower amount from taxable pension

topics.example: A widow receives a family pension of Rs. 60,000 under the default regime. 1/3rd is Rs. 20,000. Since Rs. 20,000 is less than Rs. 25,000, she gets a deduction of Rs. 20,000.
remember: Family pension deduction ceiling under default tax regime u/s 202 is Rs. 25,000.
Zero deduction is allowed against dividend income.
mistakes: Claiming interest expense incurred to earn dividend income as a deduction under IFOS.

quiz.q: What is the maximum family pension deduction under the default tax regime u/s 202?
quiz.why: Section 93 allows 1/3rd of family pension or Rs. 25,000 under the default regime, whichever is less.

quiz.q: Can collection charges paid to a bank for earning dividend income be claimed as a deduction?
quiz.why: No deduction shall be allowed in respect of any dividend income or mutual fund unit income.

topics.title: Deductions Not Allowable & Deemed Income
explain: Personal expenses of the assessee are strictly non-deductible u/s 94.
Interest or salaries payable outside India without TDS are disallowed.
30% of sum payable to a resident is disallowed if TDS is not deducted or not paid before return due date u/s 263(1).
Cash payments exceeding Rs. 10,000 (or Rs. 35,000 for transport) in a day are disallowed.
Unreasonable or excessive payments made to related persons are disallowed.
Section 95 taxes recovered amounts or cessation of liability in respect of loss/expense allowed as deduction in an earlier year as deemed income.

flow.title: Evaluating Disallowance for Resident Payments Without TDS
steps: Incur expenditure payable to a resident
Check if TDS was deducted and deposited on time
If TDS defaulted, disallow 30% of expenditure
Allow 30% deduction in year TDS is later deposited

topics.example: An assessee pays Rs. 1,00,000 for professional services under IFOS to a resident without deducting TDS. Rs. 30,000 (30%) is disallowed u/s 94.
remember: 30% disallowance for resident TDS default.
Cash payment disallowance limit is Rs. 10,000 per person per day.
mistakes: Disallowing 100% of payment to a resident for TDS default instead of the statutory 30%.

quiz.q: What percentage of expenditure payable to a resident is disallowed u/s 94 if TDS is not deducted?
quiz.why: Section 94 disallows 30% of any sum payable to a resident on which TDS has not been deducted or paid.

quiz.q: If a deduction for an expense was allowed in Year 1 and the liability is remitted in Year 3, how is it treated u/s 95?
o: Taxed as deemed income in Year 3
quiz.why: Section 95 provides that remission of liability allowed earlier as deduction is deemed income in the year of remission.
